events.title: The election of Pope St. Gregory VII
events.shortBlurb: The monk Hildebrand became pope and gave his name to a sweeping reform of the Church…
body: On 22 April 1073, at the funeral of Alexander II, the clergy and people of Rome acclaimed as pope the archdeacon Hildebrand, who took the name Gregory VII. Born at Sovana in Tuscany about the year 1015, he had long been the soul of the reforming party in the Roman Church.

His reform struck at simony and clerical marriage and, above all, at lay investiture, the appointment of bishops by secular powers. When the German king Henry IV defied him, Gregory excommunicated and deposed him in 1076; the next January the king stood barefoot in the snow as a penitent at Canossa to win absolution.

Henry renewed the war, set up an antipope, and took Rome in 1084; rescued and then ruined by his Norman allies, Gregory withdrew to Salerno and died there on 25 May 1085, saying, 'I have loved justice and hated iniquity, therefore I die in exile.' He was canonized by Benedict XIII in 1728.
